item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: A robed figure appears to personal, And will approach personal through dreams, or hallucinations. These dreams will induce fear, and paranoia until they 'Take its hand' and disappear with the SCP

Central Narrative: Incident 8227-1, Dr Christine shows extreme fear, and is eventually taken by SCP-8227. MTF Mu-13 around her talk about how she shows fear in these moments.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The whole point of SCP-8227 was to introduce mystery and uncertainty into what they are. item.title: The Phantom
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Class, containment procedures, a professional description of the SCP and what it does, followed by three incident reports.

Elevator Pitch: Put simply, SCP-XXXX is a cat-like apparition which consumes souls. It once had intangibility (Which it lost during an incident), and it can shield itself from all wavelengths of light, rendering itself invisible for a short duration.

It’s a hunter, so it stalks any kind of prey which catches its interest, though it prefers humans. It will stalk its target, memorizing all of its routines, mannerisms, and daily patterns in extreme detail. When they are at a point of vulnerability (Provided SCP-XXXX hasn’t lost interest) it will consume their soul.

After a large amount of souls are consumed, it exhales them into the form of a polychromatic sphere, which it then carries to an unidentifiable and unspecified location.

+ Show block
- Hide block

That’s how it’s going to be written, but in actuality, SCP-XXXX is bringing the sphere to a GOI (Of my creation) so they can use it to prevent some kind of cataclysmic event from occuring. The Foundation is unaware of this, and all they know is that whenever they try to take the sphere away from the SCP, several events occur:

  1. SCP-XXXX becomes extremely agitated.
  2. People start disappearing from the Foundation (They’re actually being dragged away by a hand of the SCP which actually causes the cataclysmic event.)
  3. Emergence of multiple anomalous entities appearing all over the world
  4. Cataclysmic event occurs.

Central Narrative: It’s a question of morals. The Foundation has to escort SCP outside after it creates the sphere (Which can even be a problem at times), but each time it’s outside it also does what it wants, and consumes even more souls. Even though the SCP’s job is presumably important, is it morally correct for the Foundation to just let it go around killing people?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Since the SCP has lost its intangibility and is now at odds with the Foundation, this prompts it to use its superior intelligence to resist and counteract any new containment procedures that the Foundation tries to come up with.

Additional Notes: Last time I left out a lot of details, since I was trying to summarize way too much. Hopefully this is a good balance of things. Once again, any advice is highly appreciated, and thanks in advance.

Forum thread: New SCP. Der Verlorene

One of my mild frustrations is that a work like this, when received by an internet audience of primarily working young people mostly steeped in genre fiction, is seen as extremely avant-garde when in fact it's a pale imitation of a now elderly poetic form first invented in the early 80s. What we see as the avant-garde is now hopelessly out of date. Bernstein is 70. David Antin is dead. Kenneth Goldsmith's post-digital internet utopianism became obsolete in 2015 when he was cancelled for turning Michael Brown's autopsy report into a poem. The days of looking to Twitter for art are long rotted six years on since. And it's very hard to try and find new ways of looking at the world in a post-post-digital humanistic landscape whose intelligentsia are more likely to have Invader Zim as a reference point to glom onto than any sort of brand new literary advancements, mostly as a result of childhood nostalgia steeped in the trauma of living in this late-capitalist hellscape.

This is not a criticism strictly speaking of the wiki's userbase, who are intelligent writers and readers, it's more an indictment of myself. Regardless of this poem's actual artistic worth or value as an SCP object/story, it was very stupid of me to parade it out and expect a ticker tape parade for my genius, if only because it's not very good and no one, me included, would be anywhere near the intellectual circles required to point that out with any serious authority. I just have a chronic illness where combining the SCP format, normally the denizen of funnee peanut memes and clickbait Youtube videos for children when it isn't left-wing internet urban fantasy/horror stories, with avant garde writings is endlessly fascinating. The sooner I grow out of it the smarter I will be.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5138 appears as a small grove of Japanese White Birch (Betula Platyphylla) in [REDACTED], Scotland. The anomaly always appears in autumnal colours and sheds a seemingly infinite amount of otherwise non-anomalous leaves. Walking down the grove will lead to a bamboo archway, which, when entered transports individuals to a traditional Japanese garden, hereby referred to as SCP-5138-1. The garden has been reported to evoke feelings of peace in all cases.

Deleted at -22 and three votes. Rewrite by Ayumi-san is pending.

SCP-5358 is a human male about twenty-four (24) years in age, and standing about 1.8 meters in height. Medical checkups so far have found no physical anomalies on the internal and external body of SCP-5358. IQ tests have given it a slightly above-average intelligence level of 116.

Deleted at -18 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Unihedron

+ show block
– hide block

I'm sorry to say, but this feels really incomplete. Whatever intrigue that the article brings me remains unanswered throughout to the end and quite honestly this feels like it's written by someone who doesn't understand or bothered attempting to elaborate on why being able to hack into outright anything is anomalous, or even interesting. The name drop to UIU had a reverse impact on me; instead of making me feel "wow, they could do that?" it made me go "there's no way this makes sense".

I think this suffers a case of show-don't-tell in that I'm being told how outrageous the situation is but nothing that pulls its weight and make it feel grand, rather that it's odd being delivered this way. I think the places in the article like the breach and the high cooperation level as shown could be translated into logs that are interesting to read and experience, but in its current form it really feels lacking.

FluffyDog00

+ show block
– hide block

In order for an article to work, there needs to be a strong narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and end. This has a beginning and a middle. There are no stakes, just a dude who is really good at something, and has no further character development other than that. It's boring and tasteless.

-1

item.title: A video game that kills you (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The SCP is a video game cartridge with scratched up stickers and scratched logo and title which is impossible to make out.
  • a video game cartridge that can be played on Nintendo 64, but no one1 remembers or knows about the game or the development of the game.
  • whenever a player dies in the video game, within 24 hours the player in real life would face the same fate as the player who died in the video game.

Central Narrative:
The whole idea of this SCP is that the game kills the subject the way the subject died in the video game.

When the cartridge is plugged into a regular Nintendo 64, the player will be introduced into an open-world. The place that sets the player in a city called: "Alt City", the player inside the game can virtually do ANYTHING2. The more the player plays in the city, the more the player wants to commit violence.

Whenever the player dies in the game then the tv unknowingly shuts off with no solutions fixing it. Within 24 hours the player will die in real life in the same way the player died in the game. There is no other way of avoiding death, and any attempts avoiding the death would just lead to death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is special about this SCP is because I think (I THINK! I am not certain) that this SCP is the first video game that kills anyone. (Again, I am not certain, there is probably an SCP like this. I don't know…)

Additional Notes: I would LOVE to see some criticism or feedback. Thank you!

Footnotes
1. as in people in a video game developing companies, as well as Nintendo
2. in that, they can commit any crime easily

item.title: SCP-IDEA (MITTERNACHTSONNE) 2nd ATTEMPT
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror
Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX commonly called (Midnight sun) is a:
⦁ Large 45 m dark quadrupedal aquatic life form
⦁ Similar in appearance to the prehistoric lizard known as mosasaurs
⦁ Has a Tentacle mane around the back of cranium
⦁ Travels at speeds equal or in access of 400km/h
⦁ Strength to body to ratio is 20:1
⦁ Covered in Robust Black scale armour exterior
⦁ It Can only viewed at night
⦁ Avoid direct eye contact, avoid viewing for more than 1 minute continuously
⦁ It's origins remain unknown
⦁ Was on the move until it was contained at the THE RING
⦁ Can increase area of influence

Central Narrative:
SCP was first alerted to the foundation through an agent located in NOAA(National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration), NOAA noticed a drastic change in salinity in area 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Initial expedition failed resulting in the loss of all life. Data emitted during time of expedition discovered: salinity in the water had changed and that the underwater local flora/fauna had mutated and become highly aggressive, SCP causing this was found to be also extremely aggressive and intelligent. SCP was contained at the site known as the THE RING after 3 failed expedition and considerable loss of life. Containment was achieved with the aide of new countermeasure technology such as: PUVDS ( perimeter ultra violet defence system- a defence systems which emits a strong ultra violet light deep into the water)- pinning SCP into a confined area, SPS( Sea perimeter system- a system designed to prevent the influence of SCP-XXXX from exceeding a 20km2 zone and for the salinity of water to not change outside of the zone. Loss of life was deemed acceptable to contain SCP-XXXX given its aggressiveness and intelligence and usual parameters of containment failing. SCP-XXXX full name is Leviathan der Mitternachtsonne (Leviathan of the Midnight sun) and was named by a formerly deceased Kreigsmarine U-boat/K version captain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP most dangerous ability is that it is capable of salinity conversion, which if left uncheck can cause cataclysmic change in weather, flora/fauna, disrupt oxygen levels. SCP-XXXX is also capable Phycological Physical Mutation (Able to transform a victim using their brain to mutate their body, without the need of physical contact provided certain conditions are met) creating 5 sub entities of various forms like the Gespenst(wraith). It uses this ability to great effect in order to escape its confinement.

Additional Notes: Constructive criticism is greatly appreciated.👍

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History, Action

Page Layout (Optional): Documentation and Experiment Logs

Elevator Pitch:
*Miniature Medieval Europe made out of paper.
*Inhabited by mini satient paper beings
*There are wars and conquests.
*Can communicate with humans.

Central Narrative: Field agents found a miniature castle made entirely out of white paper in the basement of an old building. They bring it back as a present for a foundation scientist. The scientist discovered one day that the castle was filled with little talking paper people. They interview the supposed "king" of this land. The castle slowly expands larger and larger, with more and more people. This scientist then proposes to make this an SCP which is granted. The tiny people refer to the scientist as their god. When a researcher accidentally brought in a red paper for unknown reasons, the red paper duplicated and became a separate empire that was enemies with the white paper empire. They are now stored separately.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't think something like this have ever been done before. It is an very interesting topic to see paper people going about their day.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello mr_tost and welcome to the Wiki! I'm a site author and member of the Community Outreach Team, and this comment is a little info list of resources that will hopefully help you with your journey through the site, both writing-wise and reading-wise. We're very happy to see new people excited to enjoy some SCP content!

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially fro when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
First, some necessary simplifications:
1) If the dimension effectively disables electronics then that makes exploring the dimension harder. While this makes uncovering its mysteries, this falls under the "too many anomalies" header, and that eliminates part of the fun. Basically, you've got a mysterious car, you have a cool dimension, that should be enough.

2) If this car is constantly challenging other cars and anyone that dies on the strip becomes another manifestation, then why do we only see the one manifestation? There should be a lot of these vehicles running around. Also, if the phantom can merely possess another vehicle when it dies then it has no fear of death.

3) Also, how do you mean "memory beyond its current vessel"? Also, how was it established?

4) You can't have the phantom as a "mysterious force" and not know if there's a driver if the force can possess others and modify vehicles. That eliminates the question one way or the other.

5) Basically, you have a lot of interesting things here, and you may have too many of them. Focus on the ones that are important to the SCP and eliminate the rest.

item.title: Two SCP green light
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Articles

Elevator Pitch: The premise is that there was a dragon and a phoenix (who both have humanoid forms) were lovers a long time ago the male is the only one who remembers and protects the female through each time she dies and is reincarnated having no memories of her previous life. Usually leading them to fall back in love. The male dislikes humans and has destroyed civilizations that have harmed/kill the female. The female loves all life and always tries to stop the male from hurting anyone.

Central Narrative: The main story part of the article would be about the foundation trying to contain the Male/Female SCP. This has multiple outcomes based on how the foundation goes about containment through each incarnation of the female. Example The foundation tries to just take the female and keep her locked up against her will leading the male to attack the site to free her, or they convince the female to come willingly and use her to contain the male which sometimes has an ok outcome. The male is immune to most forms of physical harm and can even nullify other SCPs anomalous effects if it is to protect the female or himself. The foundation becomes interested in containing the male to help contain other SCP because of his ability to nullify other effects. The male will not always just do what the female says and will even go against her wishes if he feels like he is protecting her.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The attention grabber is an ancient dragon protecting his phoenix lover that does not remember him after she dies. His raw power making containment of him or her near impossible.

Additional Notes: This is my first time writing an SCP so any feedback or advice would be appreciated.

item.title: Re: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Overall, I like it but it needs to remove some of the fuzziness. If it's a trap for the dragons, then why can they send out feelers to entice people into the trap with them? You also have the problem that it goes all over the place, no one has physical proof (as the children disappear at 1 km), and anyone who goes into the house disappears forever; this brings up the question of how The Foundation ever heard of it.

Put another way: Disappearing people could be ascribed to any number of SCPs; ascribing it specifically to one that teleports feels weird.

Another option is to explore the trap idea further. It would be interesting to see it as a trap for not just the dragons, but humans as well. In a weird way that may add to the horror as the trap isn't for the obvious aliens, but for anyone that finds it. This brings into existence a force that's actually just trapping subjects for its own means.

Overall, this is a great start but based on what we see here, needs a little additional work. Just remove some of the fuzziness and you should have a great concept.

item.title: Re: De Facto
item.content:encoded:
A decent eldritch horror, and you have both the ecological horror as well as one that puts man in its place.

The two basic problems are 1) There's no way for this to be known by The Foundation if no one escapes it. Part of being in The Foundation's catalog is that it needs to be able to study it, even if it's from afar, and there is just no opportunity for that here. This is not only an ongoing threat, and one that needs to be dealt with, but also one that just doesn't lend itself to study.

This is one that is likely to be neutralized and then studied, and that needs to be allowed for in the write-up.

The other is that there isn't much of a hook. Again, I think that if you emphasized the ecological horror you would have a better hook than that you have something infecting the local structure. You just need to tie it to something to make it even scarier.

item.title: The Railyard To Everywhere
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Horror

Elevator Pitch: The SCP (from now on referred to as the railyard) is a 1km x 300m railyard found in a pocket dimension. It is only accessible by a junction located a few miles from the Southeastern entrance of the Bradway Tunnel in South Yorkshire. Inside the yard, there are about 50 sidings and 14 entryways (9 of which lead to tunnels) and two operating facilities. Surrounding the yard is a rocky, heathland similar to those found in the UK.

On some occasion, locomotives enter the railyard via the tunnels or junctions. Locomotives of all kinds will enter and exit the railyard and will only remain to dispatch/pick up all cargo. The only locomotives permanently found within are a GWR 9400 Class and two BR Class 10.

Central Narrative: The junction was initially found in 1965 during the Beeching Axe. Reports came in of workers vanishing when they attempted to find the end of the line. The Foundation came in when a BR DMU went missing along with 37 passengers.

Across numerous expeditions, the foundation makes a number of bizarre discoveries. During one expedition, the foundation attempted to remove some of the wagon's contents. Upon doing this, the shunters became very hostile toward the personnel and attempted to prevent them from escaping the railyard. Two personnel died in the escape.

In the penultimate log, it mentions a 'smoke' engine exiting the junction, with four humans on board. Later, during an interview with one of the humans, she reveals to be one of the passengers who went missing on the BR DMU a few years before. During her interview, she described the world she and her fellow passengers were in and what they did in order to return to their reality.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: During one expedition, a 5AT1 came into the railyard and dropped off mail van. Upon inspection of mail, the foundation discovered that most of the mail was in written in Nguni languages and some had post dates of 31st of June and 32nd of October. These discoveries caused the foundation to deduce that the railyard not only connects alternative dimensions but also parallel universes.

Additional Notes: I will not do anything related to Thomas & Friends!

Footnotes
1. A steam engine only proposed in our word

item.title: Re: SCP Idea:Genie in the Music?
item.content:encoded:
Hi jpdelta6, thanks for expanding on the story. I think it's a good start, but you still have a few inconsistencies to iron out. For example:

But the cool steam it releases is a great aesthetic

How did we get from a stereo -> steam? You're stretching the imagination from the start of the narrative and might make readers ask the same question. I'd suggest sticking to the sensory domain that fits your object / entity, in this case, sound. If you want steam, then have a steam machine as the object instead.

people begin dropping like flies but none of them seem to notice things are going wrong

Clearly, someone noticed, as the club goes on operating for a while? If you want people to drop like flies, then what happens to them after? Will stopping the machine make them recover?

it can just feed of their surface consciousness not killing anyone right away

I'm guessing you're referring to the Djinn here? Perhaps you should clarify this - so it's absorbing people's consciousness? Why would it want to kill people then? Why not just make them dance forever?

It becomes more and more physical even becoming an ambiguous member of their crew but no one seems to notice.

What does this mean? The Djinn becomes a crewmember? Why? How?

Also, I want you to start thinking about how you plan on presenting this narrative in an SCP article format. It's good that you've decided, for example, to focus the story through the eyes of the surviving young man, but how will you tell his story? Will he be interviewed by the Foundation? Will there be camera/exploration logs etc.?
